title: Mapping Information-Processing Reallocation for Dependency-Restructuring Analysis: A Bounded Functional Input Procedure
content: Dependency Restructuring Analysis (Sternieri, 2026) examines how technological enactment changes requirement relations among organizational activities. Its application requires a reliable reconstruction of the informational functions performed within those activities before and after technological change. Existing process-modeling, process-mining, and human–automation function-allocation methods provide complementary analytical tools, but do not, by themselves, deliver the integrated, evidence-based input required for this specific analysis. This paper addresses that methodological gap by introducing a dedicated procedure for constructing a structured input package for Dependency Restructuring Analysis. The procedure identifies information-processing functions, establishes their correspondence across observation periods, documents their actual allocation between human and technological contributors, and distinguishes changes in execution from changes in functional identity and processing performance. It also preserves the evidence supporting each classification and explicitly identifies unresolved observations. The resulting package provides researchers and organizational analysts with a systematic, traceable, and directly usable foundation for reconstructing the informational components of activity configurations and subsequently examining organizational dependencies. An illustrative application demonstrates how the package is assembled and transferred to the subsequent analysis. Although developed specifically for Dependency Restructuring Analysis, the procedure can also support other investigations of technological change and the reconfiguration of organizational work.
